changeSummary: Add git stash (excluding list and show) and git worktree add targeting a path under .claude to the blocked-command hook. Remove Bash(git checkout *) and Bash(git add *) from settings.local.json and narrow Bash(node *) and Bash(npm run *). Extend scan-agent-config-security.mjs to read settings.local.json.
rationale: The hook is the only layer not bypassable by an allow rule or an interactive prompt. Documentation was already in place and failed. The permission file is currently invisible to every gate.
validationPlan: npm run test:claude-system passes with a new deterministic case proving git stash is blocked
A negative case proves git stash list and git stash show remain allowed
npm run security:claude reports findings for the settings.local.json allow entries before they are reduced, proving the scanner now reads the file
npm run validate:claude and npm run system:health -- --ci are not made worse by this change
security-auditor independently reviews the hook regex for over-blocking and under-blocking
rollback: Delete the added hook array entries and restore the previous settings.local.json allow list. Both are additive, few-line changes with no data migration.
risks: Over-blocking a legitimate git stash list or git stash show if the negative lookahead is wrong
Narrowed node and npm run permissions may surface more interactive prompts and slow routine work
Removing Bash(git checkout *) may block legitimate branch switching; must be assessed during the pilot
ownerApproval: Project owner explicitly approved all three parts after being shown the exact change, the cost in added permission prompts, and the required sequencing.
sequencing: Guard first. skip-worktree must not be removed until the guard is proven, because it is currently the only barrier protecting most ledgers.

changeSummary: Add a provenance predicate to assertEnglishInternalFiles in scripts/validate-claude-config.mjs so append-only machine-written evidence registries, defined as any .jsonl under .claude, plus an explicit ten-entry list of generated operational artefacts, are skipped by the English-only character rule. Add two overlay cases to scripts/test-claude-system.mjs: a positive case proving product-language evidence passes inside a registry, and a negative control proving an authored agent prompt containing the product language still fails. Add one sentence to CLAUDE.md distinguishing authored internal files from evidence registries. The product-name allowlist, the writer scripts, the CI step order and all authored configuration paths are untouched.
rationale: Recorded retrospectively after implementation and before acceptance, to comply with DEC-0004, which requires that no validation gate is narrowed without an approved and recorded proposal. The project owner approved Option A with generated-artefact coverage, and the research is RES-0002, but the proposal event was omitted at delegation time. That omission is disclosed here rather than backdated. The change is a prerequisite for removing skip-worktree from the four operational registries and committing 127 Work OS, contract and performance records, which is tracked as DEBT-0005; committing those registries without this change would break CI for real.
validationPlan: npm run validate:claude reaches 0 errors, down from 4
npm run test:claude-system passes with the new positive case and the new negative control
The negative control is mutation-verified: broadening the exemption to all of .claude must make the suite fail
The positive case is mutation-verified: removing the exemption must make the suite fail
npm run system:health -- --ci returns to 100/100 PASS from 92/100 FAIL
npm run lint, npm run build and npm test hold their baseline, with 18 backend tests passing
Exempt-path comparison normalises separators so Windows and Linux CI agree
qarga-system-reviewer independently reviews scope, security, context cost and rollback and must not be the author
security-auditor independently confirms the exemption cannot smuggle non-English instruction text into an authored prompt, skill, command or policy
rollback: Single revert across scripts/validate-claude-config.mjs, scripts/test-claude-system.mjs and CLAUDE.md. The exemption is read-side only and there is no data migration or state change.
risks: Real and deliberate narrowing of a repository-wide gate: after this change an agent can write free-form product-language prose into a ledger summary field and no gate will object

The .claude jsonl rule is a wildcard, so any future .jsonl added under .claude is exempt automatically without review; the reviewer should decide whether to replace it with an explicit eighteen-path list
The ten-entry generated-artefact list is hand maintained and will drift silently when a new generated report is added
The negative control constrains the blast radius to non-authored files; it does not constrain content within them
A second Claude session is concurrently active in this repository and previously reverted an unrecorded version of this same change; concurrent writes to append-only registries remain a live risk
ownerApproval: Project owner approved Option A with generated-artefact coverage, and separately approved Option D as a follow-up subtask, after being shown the option comparison and the residual coverage loss. The owner also confirmed DEC-0004 was genuinely owner-approved, which is why this proposal is being recorded before acceptance rather than after.
sequencing: QW-0006-S01 implements this proposal and is submitted for review. QW-0006-S02 implements Option D in the same file and starts only after S01 review is accepted. QW-0006-S03 is the independent security audit. Removing skip-worktree and committing the operational registries under DEBT-0005 happens only after S01 is accepted.
